title: The schema's worked example -- a FETCHED, normal-less triangle, and the only case that exercises the pin, the allow-list and the licence table

criterion.says: This is the simplest model that can be represented in glTF.

acceptanceClass.because: The one case in the tree that was constructed for exactness from the start: Khronos's Triangle is right-isoceles, and the camera is fronto-parallel, rolled by -arctan(1/2) so the three edges take raster slopes -1/2, 2 and 1/3, and scaled to s = 352.1 so that 5s = 1/2 (mod 1) puts all three edge constants at half a lattice step (`board/`). The whole derivation stands in scene.camera.derivation and the runner recomputes both conditions rather than trusting it. The SUBJECT is upstream's and the CAMERA is ours, which is the ownership case that makes the freedoms ours: the placement is spent through the camera.

subjects.name: Triangle
subjects.notes: No NORMAL accessor. Coverage is decided from Cycles' alpha on the oracle side and from depth != far on ours, so this comparison reads no normal at either end and none is derived: I.26 forbids deriving one and an oracle comparison contains no repair. A rung that compares RADIANCE needs a subject that carries what radiance reads, and that is a different subject.

source.pinReason: first pin; head of main at the time the ladder was written

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

camera.derivation: yfov = 2*atan((24/2)/50) from Blender's factory 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL. roll = -arctan(1/2) = -26.5650511771 deg, and the SIGN is a measurement rather than a preference: a camera roll of +r turns the camera's right vector towards its up vector, so the image of the world rotates by -r. THE ROLL IS CHOSEN FOR THE SLOPES AND NOT FOR THE ANGLES. At this roll the sample's three edges have raster slopes 1/2, 2 and 1/3, and for a slope p/q in lowest terms the distance from EVERY pixel centre in the plane to the line p*X - q*Y = c is |c - round(c)| / sqrt(p^2+q^2) -- independent of the subject's size, where an irrational slope gives about 0.5/L over L boundary pixels and shrinks as the subject grows. The maxima 0.5/sqrt(5), 0.5/sqrt(5) and 0.5/sqrt(10) = 0.223607, 0.223607 and 0.158114 px are reached where all three constants sit at half a lattice step, and THAT CONSTRAINS THE SCALE AS WELL AS THE AIM: with s = k/sqrt(5) the three constants satisfy (V0V1) + (V1V2) - (V0V2) = 5s identically, so half-lattice on all three needs 5s = 1/2 (mod 1). The plain height fit s = 352 (704 px of 720) fails it and admits at best 0.129692 px; s = 352.1 satisfies it, which is k = 352.1*sqrt(5) = 787.31953487767601 px per unit and puts the subject's rotated bounding box 704.2 px tall inside the frame's 720. The aim then follows: the first vertex must land at pixel (0.3, 0.1) modulo 1 -- the unique solution of Cx + 2Cy = 1/2 and 2Cx - Cy = 1/2 -- and the vertex nearest the frame centre that satisfies it is (463.3, 712.1), which places the other two at (1167.5, 360.0) and (111.2, 7.9), all three inside 1280x720. Distance 1.9051985039759638 m is (720/2) / (0.24 * k), the depth at which one unit subtends k px.
camera.note: THE ENGINE'S OWN ANSWER, QUOTED (board:1398). Every number here is read from the framing rule's output for this subject -- eye, aim, yfov and both clip planes -- rather than recomputed by the authoring helper, which bounded each primitive by the eight transformed corners of its local AABB and therefore always at least as loosely as the engine bounds the transformed vertices. A looser radius moves the eye back, and 93 cases declared a camera the rule does not derive. `ADerivedCameraIsTheFramingRuleAndNotAQuotation` recomputes all of it and refuses a mismatch, so what this declaration does is PIN the viewpoint, never choose it.

light.note: Rung 1 compares a coverage mask. The only illumination is Blender's factory world, which costs nothing to match and is left where it is.

world.note: Configured by not being configured. The observed colour and strength go into provenance.json, so a Blender that changed them is visible without any machinery that refuses.

material.note: Diffuse BSDF with Roughness pinned to 0, never Principled: Principled at metallic 0 still carries a specular lobe at IOR 1.5. This subject is a single unoccluded facet, which is the one shape where Cycles has no integration left and the answer is the closed form rho*L = 0.8 x 0.05087608844041824 = 0.0407008707523346 -- so this is one of the cases that keeps that number exercised (board:0087).

default.note: The binary mask. One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it. This is the recipe the acceptance numbers below are judged on.

coverage.note: The analytic pixel-area fraction: alpha over the full-width box is the coverage, and alpha = 0.5 is the edge through the pixel centre, which gives a signed sub-pixel edge offset instead of a count. Its own per-pixel alpha noise is the instrument floor and is the test's to measure -- it is not asserted here.

notes: Khronos's Triangle is the schema's worked example and never rung 1's subject (board:0078 row 1, I.26): it is out on two counts at once -- no NORMAL, and it is fetched where rung 1 requires a generated subject so that a red there has exactly one cause. It is kept because nothing else in the tree fetches anything, so without it the pin, the redirect-refusing allow-list and the per-file licence derivation have no subject at all.

subjectFrameFraction.derivation: the projected area of the subject's triangles over 1280*720 at the declared camera, recomputed by the runner from the fetched vertices; exact because the subject is a plane perpendicular to the optical axis, so its perspective image is a similarity and the area is (1/2) * k^2 / (1280*720) at k = 352.1*sqrt(5) px per unit. 33.6111 % is what the plain 704 px height fit would give, and it is 0.019 points smaller because that fit cannot carry the half-lattice condition the margins need.
subjectFrameFraction.note: What the boundary bound is applied UNDER: I.26's IoU ~ 1 - P*d/A makes P/A a property of the subject's size, so a camera that framed the subject smaller would tighten the bound without saying so. The runner recomputes this and refuses a mismatch.
